cohort: 11 Japanese singleton pregnant women with fetal growth restriction (FGR) who received tadalafil along with conventional management, matched for maternal age, parity, gestational age, and estimated fetal weight at enrollment with 14 singleton pregnant women who received only conventional management for FGR
finding: Both birthweight and fetal growth velocity from enrollment to birth were significantly higher in the tadalafil group than in the conventional management group.
mod_finding: The cesarean delivery rate was approximately twofold higher in the conventional management group than in the tadalafil group, with cesarean section due to non-reassuring fetal status performed in seven pregnant women in the conventional management group (58.3%) but in none in the tadalafil group (P < 0.05, chi-squared test).
gest_age: Not specified, but groups were matched for gestational age at enrollment
birth_weight: Birthweight was measured as an outcome
